Reposting my response:

Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).

You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.

I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.

The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:

#set specific starting values:
specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
#have at it
oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)

Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.

So, in short:

1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
3) play with starting values for sigma

Let me know how that goes!

Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).

You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.

I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.

The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:

#set specific starting values:
specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
#have at it
oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)

Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.

So, in short:

1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
3) play with starting values for sigma

Let me know how that goes!

Hi Jeff,

We are about to publish a new method for integrating telemetry data into SCR which we hope to add to oSCR sometime soon. Not soon enough for you, but if you are interested in seeing the preprint, or more specifically the code for fitting the model, let me know.

A feature of the approach is that it estimates separately a 'movement' sigma and an SCR sigma. In discussions with Dan, we wondered whether assuming they are the same value might be part of the issue folks are having.

Reposting my response:

Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).

You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.

I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.

The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:

#set specific starting values:
specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
#have at it
oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)

Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.

So, in short:

1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
3) play with starting values for sigma

On Wednesday, September 2, 2020 at 7:54:57 AM UTC-4 danl...@gmail.com wrote:
Reposting my response:

Your data looks to be formatted correctly, though 71 occasions is going to give you trouble.  That is a lot, and it might be worth playing around with the collapse.k() function and using the Poisson encounter model.  Then, for variable trap operation you can develop an "effort" covariate on p0 that is log(days) for each trap.  This will be a much faster approximation that could be effective if you don't have important occasion-specific covariates (e.g., weather).

You are correct that RSF=F indicates you only want sigma help from the telemetry, and using rsfDF = ssDF is usually reasonable.

I would still divide by 1e3, converting your UTMs into kilometer units.  Your mmdm/mdm are then 1.7/5.6 which are more friendly to the optimizer.

The error you are seeing is unfortunately the biggest struggle with this integration approach -- the telemetry data suggest a very different sigma than the trap data (usually larger).  In oSCR, the starting value according to the trap data uses a default of log(mmdm*0.5).  The way to combat this is by using a custom starting value:

#set specific starting values:
specific.starts <- c("sig.(Intercept)" = 5)
#have at it
oSCR.fit(mod, scrFrame = data$sf,ssDF = data$ssDF, start.vals = specific.starts)

Here, I've told the model to try a sigma of exp(5) = 148 units, which is likely too big (if in kilometers).  But, the larger value could work better depending on the telemetry data.  In your case, with 100m units and an mmdm of 17.4, your sigma starting value would automatically be 2.16.

So, in short:

1) try collapsing the k occasions and fitting a Poisson encounter model
2) divide meters by 1e3 to get km
3) play with starting values for sigma

Let me know how that goes!
